note: Hand-verified callers/callees of stable functions/methods in crates/cli/src/{decompress,human}.rs, read directly from source (not echoed from the graph). Scope = INTRA-REPO call targets only: calls into std and external crates (globset, std::env, Path/PathBuf) have no graph node and are excluded, so a missing edge reflects a real resolution gap, not an out-of-corpus call. Peer keys are <package-path>.<qualified-name>; Rust package paths are '::'-separated and carry no '/', so trace.peerKey keeps the full path (e.g. crates::cli::src::human.ParseSizeError.format). Three cross-language signal probes isolate what the name-resolution tree-sitter extractor drops vs go/types: (a) calls inside closures — ParseSizeError::int/overflow live in map_err/ok_or_else closures (parse_human_readable_size), CommandError::io lives in map_err closures (DecompressionMatcherBuilder.build); (b) instance dispatch on a chained typed value — DecompressionMatcherBuilder::new().build() in DecompressionMatcher::new drops the .build() leg. #468 (uniform tree-sitter tags) aims to recover these. Scored via: dex bench trace run --project <ripgrep> --gold benchmark/trace/ripgrep-rust.json
